html:
The Oneida, or Onyota'a:ka, "People of the Standing Stone", are one of the five founding nations of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy. In 1492 they lived in central New York, south of Oneida Lake, between the Mohawk to the east and the Onondaga to the west.

Like the other Iroquois nations they lived in longhouse villages and grew maize, beans and squash. In the American Revolution most Oneida, unlike most of the Confederacy, sided with the Americans. They fought at the Battle of Oriskany in 1777 against other Haudenosaunee, which split the League.

Treaties after the war still cost them most of their land. In the 1820s and 1830s many Oneida moved to Wisconsin, and in the 1840s others moved to Ontario, on the Thames River. A third group, the Oneida Indian Nation, remains in New York and won back some land in the late 1900s.
